about: Shetach territories and heads over time, the United States first (the owner's idea, Nov 6; started Nov 8). It holds what a map of any year needs: whose shetach each area was in, and who headed each shetach. 'areas' is keyed by the map's piece id, '<state>:<shetach id>' as in web/data/centers.geojson ('US-OR:oregon' is Oregon, 'US-OH:michigan' the Toledo area, 'US-WV:western-pennsylvania' West Virginia). Its periods run oldest first: from a period's 'from' until the next period's 'from', the area was part of that period's 'shetach', given by the id in data/shetachim.json of that head's shetach today (Levitin's Pacific Northwest is 'washington'). Before the first period the area was in no shetach, as far as is known. 'heads' is keyed by shetach id: its heads, oldest first, each {head, from, name (what the shetach was called then, where it differs)}; a shetach with one head since it began lists him from its start, with the sources on the area period that starts it. 'events' is keyed by shetach id: vaads, passings and the like, each {date, what, sources}. Dates are 'YYYY', 'YYYY-MM' or 'YYYY-MM-DD'; when only bounds are known, 'from' is null and 'fromBound' is {after, by}. 'how': owner (the owner's own statement, taken as fact; owner, Nov 8: "I'm telling you as a fact ... I just need to figure out when each one split off. Stop trying to verify my facts"), stated (a source states it), news (a report from the time), anniversary (counted back), range (only bounds). 'confidence', as in data/founding-years.json: high (a report from the time, or the shetach's own statement, and nothing against it), medium (one later source, a count back, or sources a year apart), low, range, open; none on 'owner' periods. 'sources': [{url, title, date (the source's own), quote (its words), via (where an earlier session found it), note}]. When an area was in another head's shetach before its own (the owner, Nov 8): "usually I would assume it was only theirs if they were doing some sort of activity there or if they were explicitly sent to those names places by the Rebbe or merkoz like how levitin was sent to all those places". Research notes: work/shetach-history/README.md.

florida.what: Rabbi Avrohom Korf's letter (dated Yud Shvat 5780) names a seven-member Vaad Hashluchim to represent him "in all aspects of Shlichus in the state of Florida" and says he will "defer all decisions to them and will accept their decisions as final"; in a follow-up email: "I would never give up my Shlichus". A vaad had been set up a few months before; this named its members.

sources.title: Florida Head Shliach Clarifies Abdicating His Role (COLlive)
New Vaad Appointed To Help Oversee Chabad Activities In Florida (CrownHeights.info)
sources.quote: Rabbi Korf notes that the Vaads decisions in matters of placement of new Shluchim, contracts between Shluchim, arbitration, and uniform codes will be final.

florida.what: Rabbi Avrohom Korf passed away (12 Tammuz 5785).
At the Florida kinus, at the shloshim, Merkos names his son Rabbi Bentzion (Benjy) Korf head shliach (heads.florida).

new-jersey.what: New Jersey's first vaad: one member 'was appointed to New Jersey's original Vaad 15 years ago' (June 2025), so about 2010.

sources.title: New Vaad Hashluchim Elected in New Jersey (Anash.org)

new-jersey.what: Rabbi Moshe Herson passed away (23 Teves 5785).
A new five-member Vaad Hashluchim is elected to serve alongside Rabbi Mendy Herson.

virginia.what: Rabbi Yaakov Noach (Yankel) Kranz passed away (6 Elul 5751); in Sept 2011 Richmond marked '20 years since the passing'.

southern-ohio.what: Kalmanson removed as head shliach (owner, Nov 8: "Kalmanson was kicked off the year after gimmel tammuz").
His organization kept the name: the JTA, on the Supreme Court's order allowing the menorah in Cincinnati's Fountain Square, calls him 'regional director of Chabad of Southern Ohio'.

sources.title: U.S. Supreme Court Intervenes to Allow Menorah in Cincinnati (JTA)

northeast-ohio.what: Rabbi Leibel Alevsky passed away (3 Iyar 5786).
